content: Skin cancer is a malignant growth that occurs on the skin and can arise from various causes. It typically develops in the epidermis, which is the outermost layer of the skin, making tumors generally visible to the naked eye. This visibility allows for early detection in most cases. There are three primary types of skin cancer, each named after the specific type of skin cell from which it originates. Skin cancers caused by ultraviolet (UV) radiation exposure can often be prevented by minimizing exposure to sunlight or artificial UV sources, wearing sun-protective clothing, and applying broad-spectrum sunscreen. Skin cancer is the fastest-growing type of cancer in the United States and is the most commonly diagnosed malignancy, surpassing lung, breast, colorectal, and prostate cancers. In 2007, it was estimated that over one million Americans would be diagnosed with skin cancer. The most common types of skin cancer are basal cell carcinoma (BCC) and squamous cell carcinoma (SCC). While these cancers can cause local disfigurement, they are generally unlikely to metastasize, meaning they rarely spread to other parts of the body. The most dangerous form of skin cancer is malignant melanoma. If not treated early, malignant melanoma can be fatal. However, it accounts for only a small percentage of all skin cancer cases.
